author: Vox
description:
Getting divorced in some states isn’t as easy as you’d think. There are separation requirements, and oftentimes people have to prove beyond a reasonable doubt that they meet certain criteria for leaving their spouse — which can rack up a significant amount of money in legal fees. 

Influencers Hadley Fairley and Jen Hamilton have taken to their social media accounts to talk openly about their divorces — and the difficulties they faced in getting them finalized.

author: Vox
description:
Pseudoscience often focuses on ideas that are easy to pay attention to: aliens building the pyramids, secret discoveries, and hidden truths being kept from the public. Those claims make better stories than the slower, less dramatic reality of how science usually works.

On this week’s episode of Unexplainable, science internet guy Hank Green talks to us about why our brains find sensational explanations so compelling, even when the evidence is weak.

author: Vox
description:
Sigmund Freud is probably the most famous psychoanalyst. Yet many of his theories have been critiqued or discredited. So is there anything we can still learn from the father of psychoanalysis?

Subscribe to our channel! http://goo.gl/0bsAjO

In today’s episode Sean speaks with professor Mark Solms, author of The Only Cure: Freud and the Neuroscience of Mental Healing. Mark argues that while Freud may have been wrong about many things, he was right about one important thing: the human mind cannot be fully understood on purely biological terms. He believes that modern psychiatry has become focused on treating mental suffering like a chemical problem, instead of focusing on emotional and psychological aspects.

Sean and Mark discuss the conscious versus the unconscious mind, whether psychoanalysis is the best therapy, and why Freud is still relevant today.

Coral reefs are incredibly important for protecting shorelines, supporting wildlife, and maintaining fisheries. But rising temperatures are threatening reefs, which could result in us losing 70% to 90% of them. One scientist says we need to move faster if we want to save them.
